rev.summary: I found no bugs in either template. The dev-theme copies of templates/llms.txt.liquid and templates/robots.txt.liquid are byte-identical to the local files (I pulled them into work/impl-review/pull), so the preview renders are valid evidence. The .ro llms.txt starts exactly with "# Alessandro Design", ends with one LF, and has no CR, BOM, stray Liquid or trailing whitespace. robots.txt is LF-only, with one blank line between groups. Its 7 groups have exactly the same directives as live. The two comment lines appear only on .ro and are the only difference from .eu apart from the host. Every .ro host variant, including the myshopify domain, 301-redirects to https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt, so none of them gets the English pointer. The else-branch links all return 200, and pointing UCP discovery at .ro matches Shopify's own default. There are two real problems, both about git and deploy rather than the templates. (1) Major: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means any later checkout or merge turns both files back into CRLF. Shopify CLI uploads files byte-for-byte, so the next push brings the CR separators back. (2) Minor: the live theme syncs with GitHub branch aless, so the push creates a shopify[bot] commit there that clashes with the uncommitted copies on daniel. I used 5 live storefront requests, spaced 3 s apart, plus one read-only theme pull.

findings.problem: Nothing keeps these two files LF in git. core.autocrlf=true is set system-wide and the repo has no .gitattributes. As soon as git rewrites the files in the working tree (checkout/switch, stash pop, reset --hard, merging the shopify[bot] sync commit from origin/aless, a fresh clone), both come back as CRLF. Shopify CLI uploads the working-tree bytes unchanged, so the next `theme push --only templates/robots.txt.liquid` brings the lone-CR robots.txt separators back live. The same would give llms.txt CRLF line endings. The working tree is LF right now, so this deploy is fine; the risk is the next edit or push.
findings.evidence: `git config --show-origin core.autocrlf` gives `file:C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig true`, and .gitattributes does not exist. `git ls-files --eol templates/robots.txt.liquid` gives `i/crlf w/lf attr/`: HEAD still holds the CRLF blob committed by shopify[bot] f46395ca on 2026-07-20. Of the 7680 files stored as i/lf, 7624 are w/crlf in the working tree, so checkouts write CRLF. In a throwaway repo with autocrlf=true (work/impl-review/eol-sim, since removed) I committed the LF versions and checked them out again: robots.txt.liquid came back with 17 CRLF out of 17 lines and llms.txt.liquid with 281 of 281. The CLI uploads CRLF unchanged: snippets/alc-seo-head.liquid is LF in piersicar commit 701c876b (normalized md5 1a535a5c) but has 159 CRLF in the matching shopify[bot] sync commit 48f8b2c6 (same md5), which means the push sent CRLF bytes.
findings.fix: Add a root .gitattributes with `templates/robots.txt.liquid text eol=lf` and `templates/llms.txt.liquid text eol=lf` (or `templates/*.txt.liquid text eol=lf`, which also covers a future llms-full.txt). Commit it in the same commit as the two templates: `git add .gitattributes templates/robots.txt.liquid templates/llms.txt.liquid`; with the attribute set, the add stores LF and replaces the CRLF blob. I checked this without committing. With the rule loaded through `git -c core.attributesFile=...`, `check-attr` reports `text: set, eol: lf` and `ls-files --eol` shows `attr/text eol=lf`. In the throwaway repo, checking out with the rule gave 0 CRLF. Theme push and the GitHub integration ignore root non-theme files; the repo already tracks package.json and node_modules at the root. Before any future push of these files, confirm `git ls-files --eol` shows w/lf.

findings.problem: The live theme 158031413515 syncs with GitHub branch `aless`. The CLI push will create a shopify[bot] commit ('Update from Shopify for theme dawn/aless') on origin/aless containing robots.txt.liquid and the new llms.txt.liquid. Both are still uncommitted on `daniel`. Merging or pulling origin/aless into daniel will then fail: 'untracked working tree file would be overwritten' for llms.txt.liquid and 'local changes would be overwritten' for robots. The usual workaround, stash + merge + pop, rewrites the files and, without F1's fix, turns them CRLF. Also, any later GitHub push to aless that lacks the new file or still has the old CRLF robots.txt.liquid will be synced back to live.
findings.evidence: `git ls-remote origin aless` = 3c3bc6c6 = local aless. The latest aless commits are shopify[bot] syncs (3c3bc6c6, 604ce08d, 1c2f2939, 48f8b2c6) made right after CLI pushes. Their files, sections/alc-breadcrumbs.liquid and snippets/alc-product-schema.liquid, still show as ` M` on daniel in `git status`, so this pattern already exists. The aless blob of templates/robots.txt.liquid is CRLF (starts `{% for group in robots.default_groups %}\r\n`).
findings.fix: Commit the two templates plus .gitattributes on daniel before, or right after, the push. Then fetch and merge origin/aless into daniel; the bot commit has identical LF content, so the merge is clean. Then push daniel's history to aless so GitHub and live stay the same. Do not push an older aless to GitHub after the deploy.

checked: The dev theme 181808693515 copies match the local files byte for byte (`shopify theme pull --only` into seo/llms-txt/work/impl-review/pull, then `cmp`), so the devtest renders are valid evidence for the local files.

ro-llms.body (13585 B) starts with b'# Alessandro Design\n\n> ' and ends with exactly one LF. It has no CR, BOM, tabs, trailing spaces, triple newlines, or leftover '{{', '%}', 'endcomment' or 'Overrides' text. It is byte-identical to seo/llms-txt/llms.ro.rendered.txt.
The agents.* values in the .ro 'Agenți AI' section render as https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/agents.md, /.well-known/ucp and /sitemap.xml. All three are in final-urlcheck.json with status 200.
eu-llms.body and hu-llms.body (320 B each) start with '# Alessandro Design', are LF-only and end with one LF. agents.store_name renders correctly.

ro-robots.body has 0 CR, 170 LF, no indented lines, at most one blank line between groups, and ends with 'Crawl-delay: 1

# LLMs.txt
# https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt
'. eu-robots.body has no comment lines and ends 'Crawl-delay: 1
', same as live.

Directive-level parse: live robots.ro.txt and the new ro-robots.body have 7 identical groups with identical user-agents, rules and order. The only text differences are that filter.v lost its 4-space indent and the extra LF from the former CRLF, plus the two trailing comments. ro-robots minus the two comment lines is byte-identical to eu-robots with the host swapped. The leading '\n' at the start of the file was already there on live and is harmless.

RFC 9309 and Google: a comment-only line is '*WS comment NL', which counts as an empty line in the grammar, so it is allowed after the last group and has no effect on the Pinterest group or any other group. Removing the leading whitespace on the filter.v line and switching to LF change no rule.

Host coverage on live (4 requests, 3 s apart, browser UA, redirects not followed): https://alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt, http://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt and https://d8cgqq-8s.myshopify.com/llms.txt each return 301 to https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt. http://alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt returns 301 to https://alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt, which then redirects to www. No .ro variant renders the else branch. hreflang lists no other .ro-market domain.

Else-branch links: .eu /agents.md returns 200 text/markdown (preview), live https://www.alessandrodesign.eu/sitemap.xml returns 200 with a sitemap index of .eu URLs, and .ro /.well-known/ucp returns 200.

UCP discovery on .ro is consistent with Shopify: the Shopify-generated agents.md and llms.txt on .eu and .hu also point Discovery, MCP endpoint and policy URLs at www.alessandrodesign.ro. Only the policy labels are translated.

Caching: live /llms.txt already returns CF-Cache-Status DYNAMIC and cdn-cache-control no-cache, no-store with an ETag of page_cache:...:LlmsTxtController:<hash>. The Shopify default body already differs per host (localized labels on .eu/.hu), so the page cache is keyed per host and locale. Host-dependent output is safe and should need no purge after the push; a single GET on .ro and .eu afterwards confirms it.

The CLI accepts the new template file: the dev theme holds templates/llms.txt.liquid, and theme-check's UndefinedObject 'agents' warnings (probe in work/r3-cli) are only warnings and don't affect a push. The theme editor saves only JSON and config files, so it cannot overwrite either template.
/agents.md and /llms-full.txt keep Shopify's default: ro-llmsfull.body and ro-agents.body are the Shopify-generated 'Agent Instructions' document.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. Every link in the chain checks out:
- **Git config:** `core.autocrlf=true` comes from C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig. There is no .gitattributes and no .git/info/attributes. `git ls-files --eol templates/robots.txt.liquid` gives `i/crlf w/lf attr/`, and llms.txt.liquid is untracked.
- **Simulation** (work/f1-verify, since removed):
  - Committing the LF robots template and checking it out again gave CRLF.
  - A plain `git stash` + `stash pop` of the current uncommitted LF file gave 17 CRs, and git warns "LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it".
  - With `templates/*.txt.liquid text eol=lf` committed, re-checkout gave 0 CRs in both templates.
- **CLI 4.8.0 source** (chunk-7T6M7FAC.js): the upload sends `value` as the raw file read. Only the checksum (`de`/`pn`) runs `replace(/\r\n/g,"\n")` for .liquid files.
- **Sync commit:** shopify[bot] 48f8b2c6 holds alc-seo-head.liquid with 159 CRs and the same normalized md5 (1a535a5c) as the LF blob in 701c876b. So pushes send the CRLF working-tree bytes.
- **Live:** one request to https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/robots.txt returned 167 CR and 1 LF (lone-CR separators). The LF template on the dev theme renders 170 LF and 0 CR.
- **Root file is safe:** the Shopify-connected branch origin/aless already tracks many root non-theme files (package.json, node_modules, CLAUDE.md, *.svg), so a root .gitattributes is harmless.

Corrections that lower the severity from major:
1. **A push alone does not bring it back.** The CLI checksum normalizes CRLF, and push only uploads files whose checksum differs from the remote (`Le` in chunk-742XXXGL.js). Once LF is live, a working copy that flipped to CRLF but has the same content is skipped. A regression needs a git rewrite plus a later content edit that gets pushed. The template changes rarely (commits on 2025-01-05 and 2026-07-20).
2. **The effect is limited.** RFC 9309 defines EOL as LF / CR / CRLF, and Google's parser accepts lone CR. A regression only brings back today's state, which matters to auditors and naive parsers, not to Google or Bing. For llms.txt, CRLF output would be harmless to consumers; whether lone CRs would appear is untested.
3. **The finding understates the near-term risk.** "This deploy is fine" holds only if nothing touches the working tree before the live push. The change is still uncommitted. The reflog shows 4 `reset: moving to HEAD` entries (stash-type resets) between 3 and 8 Sep, and the stash+pop simulation above turned the LF file into CRLF. A live `--only` push after that would upload CRLF, because the content differs from live.

Result: real, but a latent, low-impact process risk. That makes it minor, not major. The proposed fix is correct and minimal.
verdict.better_fix:
1. Add a root .gitattributes containing `templates/*.txt.liquid text eol=lf`.
2. Commit it together with the two templates before any stash, branch switch or reset. A .gitattributes left untracked does not protect during `git stash -u`: in the simulation the pop still wrote CRLF.
3. Right before the live `shopify theme push --only templates/robots.txt.liquid --only templates/llms.txt.liquid`, byte-check the working files. Both `tr -cd '\r' < templates/robots.txt.liquid | wc -c` and the same for llms.txt.liquid must print 0. `git ls-files --eol` should show `w/lf`.
4. Keep that byte check as the real guard. The attribute stops git-caused rewrites but not an editor saving CRLF; in the simulation git only flags that as modified.
5. After a content-changing live push, confirm the live robots.txt has 0 CR bytes. A later LF-only re-push with identical content may be skipped by the CLI checksum comparison.

verdict.reasoning:
Some facts in the finding are correct. `aless` is made of shopify[bot] "Update from Shopify for theme dawn/aless" commits that land right after CLI pushes. `templates/llms.txt.liquid` is not on `aless`. The `aless` robots.txt.liquid blob has CRLF (12 CRs; the index also shows i/crlf). The working-tree copies of alc-breadcrumbs and alc-product-schema match `aless` exactly when CR is ignored. The conclusions drawn from those facts don't hold up:

1. Nobody merges `aless` into `daniel` here. `daniel` was created from `aless` on 2 Sep 2026 (reflog: "branch: Created from aless", merge-base 5b2611c5). Since then it has had 0 merges, and the branches have split 28/42. The local `aless` is only moved by fast-forward updates ("aless@{2026-09-12}: pull: fast-forward"). None of those updates appears in HEAD's reflog, so the working tree on `daniel` is never touched. The project memory (live-theme-deploy.md) also says never to merge between the two branches because of CRLF churn and an incomplete mirror.

2. That merge is already broken, with or without this change. A read-only `git merge-tree --write-tree daniel aless` exits 1 with 39 conflicts, including theme.liquid, locales/ro.json, index.json and several collection.*.json files. Most come from CRLF-vs-LF differences and theme-editor JSON. Output is saved in seo/llms-txt/work/f2-verify/mergetree.txt. So the claim "the bot commit has identical LF content, so the merge is clean" is false. Two more files that git refuses to overwrite add nothing real. That refusal is a safe abort that loses no data.

3. The "later GitHub push to aless" risk also doesn't hold. A normal push to `aless` must fast-forward onto the bot commit, so it would include llms.txt.liquid and the LF robots file. Only a force-push of an old `aless` could bring back the old state, and that is true of every deploy, not something this change adds. Kanghu's direct commits on `aless` are GitHub web edits made on top of the current tip.

4. The proposed fix is harmful. Merging origin/aless into `daniel` and then pushing `daniel` to `aless` would trigger the GitHub-to-live sync for every file that differs. That includes templates/index.json, collection.*.json, page.author.json and the locales. It would overwrite theme-editor edits on the live theme, which the deploy rule forbids ("never push templates/*.json wholesale"). It also means resolving 39 conflicts, and any mistake would go straight to production.

The only valid point left is ordinary hygiene: commit the two templates on `daniel` eventually. That has no practical effect on the deploy.
verdict.better_fix: No action needed for this deploy. After the CLI push, commit templates/llms.txt.liquid and templates/robots.txt.liquid on `daniel` as usual; the line-ending question is F1's .gitattributes fix. Do not merge origin/aless into `daniel`, and do not push `daniel` to `aless`, because GitHub would sync `daniel`'s templates/*.json and locales to live.

rev.summary:
I found no wrong URL mappings and no unintended changes. I recomputed the DWF-to-final diff from seo/llms-txt/dwf-llms.txt against work/devtest/ro-llms.body and it matches dwf-vs-final.diff exactly. The changes are:
- 34 link lines where only the URL changed; every label is untouched.
- The "Parteneriate" line removed.
- The privacy and cookie lines merged into one, and a refund-policy line added.
- A showroom link added.
- "Telefon alternativ" relabelled "WhatsApp", and the full street address added to the showroom line.
- A new "Agenți AI" section.
- A final newline added.

Everything else is byte-identical: no CR, no BOM, no trailing spaces, and only comma-below ș/ț. The Romanian text in templates/llms.txt.liquid matches the render; only the three agents.* Liquid tags differ. Every URL replacement is backed by v1-urls/v1b-recheck, where the target's h1 or title matches the live menu label. I re-checked the five named targets today:
- **lustre-cu-bec:** h1 "Lustre".
- **lustre-metalice:** h1 "Lustre Industrial".
- **oglinzi-baie-cu-led-si-dezaburire:** title "Oglinzi LED Multifunctionale", 155 anti-fog mirrors.
- **instalatii:** h1 "Instalatii Exterior", 3 outdoor IP65 light strings.
- **copac-artificial:** h1 "Copac artificial", 32 trees.

The new factual lines also check out on the live site:
- WhatsApp 0730.478.880 is in the footer and on /pages/contact.
- /pages/contact gives the address as Bulevardul Voluntari 108bis, Voluntari, Ilfov.
- The footer cookie link goes to /policies/privacy-policy.
- /pages/showroom and /policies/refund-policy both return 200 and are self-canonical.

What is left is one small spelling fix ("cookies") and six business-fact problems for the client to decide. Two of them matter most: the site-wide showroom renovation banner, and the Decorațiuni category where all 21 products are sold out. The others are conflicting WhatsApp numbers, a "Lustre Industrial" collection that holds almost no industrial chandeliers, manufacturer-vs-retailer wording, and linked sources that contradict each other. I made 17 paced requests (at least 2.5 s apart, browser UA) to www.alessandrodesign.ro and saved the scratch files in seo/llms-txt/work/content-review/.

findings.problem: Needs client decision. The file says in the present tense that customers can visit the Voluntari showroom. The final version makes this more prominent: it adds a [Showroom Voluntari] link (body line 216) and the full street address (line 240). Meanwhile every page of the site says the showroom will close for renovation, with no dates, and the site's own opening hours conflict. An AI assistant could send a customer to a closed showroom.
findings.evidence: Fresh fetches 2026-09-14 10:11-10:12Z: the announcement bar on every page (/collections/*, /pages/contact, /pages/showroom, /policies/*) reads 'Showroomul din Voluntari va fi inchis pentru renovari.' and links to /pages/showroom. /pages/showroom (fresh 10:12:53Z) gives no renovation dates, no street address and no h1. Its hours are 'Luni - Vineri: 09:00 - 18:00 / Sambata: 09:00 - 15:00 / Duminica: Inchis'. Help Center article 5430 (v2b-recheck/help-articles-cached.md line 1396) says 'Duminică 09:00 – 15:00'. The footer says 'Showroom Voluntari: L-V: 9-18; S: 9-15'.
findings.fix: Ask the client for the renovation status and dates, then pick one of two options. (a) If a closure is planned or ongoing, add this under '## Showroom' in templates/llms.txt.liquid (template lines 220-226): 'Showroomul din Voluntari va fi închis temporar pentru renovare (perioada: <date confirmate>); verificați https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/pages/showroom înaintea vizitei.' (b) If the banner is stale, have the client remove it. Either way, the Sunday hours in Help article 5430 should be corrected. Until the client answers, the file should not state that the showroom is currently open.

findings.problem: Needs client decision. The file presents decorations as a core specialty: the opening summary and line 13, 'Categorii principale', a whole '## Decorațiuni' section, and 'Pagini importante'. But every product in that category is sold out, so an AI would recommend products no one can buy. 'Sifoane de pardoseală' has the same problem.
findings.evidence: Fresh /collections/decoratiuni-perete/products.json (10:12:58Z): 21 products, 0 available; product types are Tablou LED 14 and Tablou Sticla 7. final-urlcheck.json: tablou-led 'products=14 available=0', tablou-sticla 'products=7 available=0', sifon-pardoseala 'products=1 available=0'. v1b-recheck confirms that the rendered pages show 'Stoc epuizat'. Decorations are mentioned or linked at body lines 3, 13, 21, 136-142 and 262; the drain line is 121.
findings.fix: Client choice: restock, or remove decorations from the file. Removing means deleting 'și decorațiuni' from lines 3 and 13, the 'Decorațiuni perete' lines 21 and 262, and the whole '## Decorațiuni' section (lines 136-142). Also drop line 121 'Sifoane de pardoseală'. In the template these are lines 9, 19, 27, 268, 142-148 and 127. The URLs themselves are valid, so this is a business decision, not a link fix.

findings.problem: Needs client decision. The new line 'WhatsApp: 0730.478.880' matches the footer and /pages/contact, but other official pages give different numbers. An agent that follows the file's own Contact or Help Center links will find conflicting WhatsApp numbers, and a stale closure note on the contact page.
findings.evidence: Fresh /pages/contact (10:12:47Z): 'WhatsApp: +40.730.478.880'; the footer says '0730.478.880'. The same page still shows 'Închis: 23.12.2024 – 07.01.2025'. Fresh /policies/contact-information (10:12:50Z), which the footer links from every page: 'Whatsapp: 0723029676'. Help Center articles 11296 and 11312: 'WhatsApp: **0723 029 676**'. /pages/dropshipment uses wa.me/+40725665925. The Organization JSON-LD publishes telephone 0720159149 (v2b-recheck).
findings.fix: The client confirms which WhatsApp number is current. If it is 0730.478.880, keep body line 238 (template 244) and have the client update the Shopify contact-information policy, Help articles 11296 and 11312, and the store phone setting that feeds the JSON-LD. The client should also remove the expired 23.12.2024–07.01.2025 note from /pages/contact. If 0723 029 676 is current, change line 238 to that number.

findings.problem: Needs client decision. Mapping 'Lustre industriale' to /collections/lustre-metalice is right as far as the site goes: the menu label, title and h1 all say 'Lustre Industrial', and none of the 129 collection handles is a better match. But the collection contains almost no industrial chandeliers, so an AI would point customers looking for industrial styles at modern LED chandeliers with remotes.
findings.evidence: Fresh /collections/lustre-metalice/products.json, pages 1-3 (10:11:32Z, 10:12:16Z, 10:12:19Z): 715 products. Only 2 have product_type 'Lustre Industrial' and 3 mention 'industrial' in the title or tags. 416 are 'Lustre LED cu Telecomanda', 91 'Lustre LED', 58 'Lustra LED', 43 'Lustre LED Cristal'. Across the store 37 products have type 'Lustre Industrial' (v2-facts/products/all.json), and 15 of them are in the first 250 products of lustre-cu-bec.
findings.fix: Client choice: (a) change the collection's conditions, e.g. product_type = 'Lustre Industrial', or retitle it on the site. (b) Until then, drop body line 51, or relabel it to what the collection actually holds, e.g. '- [Lustre metalice](https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/collections/lustre-metalice)' (template line 57).

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the main point, but "major" is too high.

What checks out:
- **Banner is live.** I fetched https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/pages/showroom at 2026-09-14T10:18:31Z (saved in seo/llms-txt/work/verify-f1/showroom.body). It still shows the banner "Showroomul din Voluntari va fi inchis pentru renovari.". The text comes from sections/header-group.json (announcement_PeptB3), so it appears on every page. The main content still gives normal hours with "Duminica: Inchis".
- **The closure looks ongoing, not planned.** The git history of sections/header-group.json shows a series of extensions:
  - 15 May: "In perioada 16 - 30 Mai ... inchis pentru renovari"
  - 2 Jun: "16 Mai - 30 Iunie", then "Doar ridicarea comenzilor este posibila"
  - 8 Jun: "8 - 20 iunie"; 19 Jun: "8 - 30 iunie"
  - 29 Jun: dates removed
  - 4 Jul: "pana pe 1 August"
  - 31 Jul (commit 7760c82b, the day before that end date): the end date was removed
  
  So the showroom has most likely been closed since mid-May with no known reopening date. The client still has to confirm.
- **The change adds detail.** In seo/llms-txt/dwf-vs-final.diff the DWF file had only "- Showroom: Voluntari, România". The final adds the [Showroom Voluntari] link (ro-llms.body line 216) and "Bulevardul Voluntari 108bis, Voluntari, Ilfov, România" (line 240). That makes a visit easier to act on.

Why only minor:
1. **The file already hedges.** Line 218 only says the showroom exists and what customers can do there, with no hours and no "open now". Line 220 already says "Informațiile privind programul showroomului ... trebuie verificate pe site înaintea vizitei."
2. **The file matches the rest of the site.** The showroom page, the footer ("Showroom Voluntari: L-V: 9-18; S: 9-15") and Help Center article 5430 ("Showroom-ul este deschis tuturor", with the 108 BIS address) all say the same thing. AI tools index those pages far more than /llms.txt. The new file adds a small amount of risk; it does not create the conflict.
3. **Out of scope.** Opening hours are not in the llms.txt at all, so the Sunday-hours error in article 5430 is a separate Help Center fix. The missing h1 on /pages/showroom is also unrelated.

Problem with fix (a): it hard-codes renovation dates in a theme file. The banner dates changed 6 times in about 11 weeks, and each llms.txt update needs a theme push, so hard-coded dates would quickly be wrong. The template also cannot read the banner automatically, because llms.txt.liquid only has access to the request and agents objects.
verdict.better_fix: Don't hard-code dates. In templates/llms.txt.liquid, replace the hedge line at template line 226 (ro-llms.body line 220) with a line that mentions a possible temporary closure and names a way to check, e.g.: "Showroomul poate fi închis temporar (de exemplu pentru renovare); înaintea unei vizite verificați anunțul de pe https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/pages/showroom sau sunați la 021.555.7252." Keep the link and the address. Separately, ask the client whether the renovation closure (banner since 16 May, end date removed 31 Jul) is still in effect. If it is, the fuller fix is on the site: add the closure notice to the /pages/showroom content, the footer and Help article 5430 (and correct Sunday to "Închis" there). If the banner is stale, have them disable it. Neither step needs a theme code change beyond the one line above.

verified.fix: The client confirms the wording and the factory year. Suggested replacement for body line 13 (template 19), from v2b-recheck: 'Alessandro Design este brandul S.C. Atlantic Logistic Concept S.R.L. (CUI RO43286659), care vinde online corpuri de iluminat, oglinzi LED, produse pentru baie, plante artificiale și decorațiuni. Potrivit site-ului, corpurile de iluminat Alessandro Design sunt produse în fabrica proprie din Guzhen (China); oferta include și oglinzi LED și produse de baie din colecțiile Marcello Funghi și Korman Technik.'

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds up, but it overstates the problem. It is a gap in positioning, not a factual error or an implementation bug.

What I confirmed:
- ro-llms.body line 3 calls the company "magazin online ... specializat".
- It uses "comercializează" on lines 13, 43 and 104. The finding only cites 3 and 13, but line 43 ("comercializează corpuri de iluminat") is the one that clashes most with the factory claim, since the site says the factory makes the lighting.
- The file never mentions a factory and does not link /pages/fabrica-alessandro-design.
- The site does push the manufacturer angle hard. /pages/companie lists "Producatori, NU comercianti." as a company value, and the factory page (Guzhen, "Din 2023") says it makes all "Alessandro Design" lighting.
- snippets/alc-product-benefits.liquid prints "Producator direct: vezi fabrica" (ro.json price_info / price_info_link) on every product page, in all locales.
- products.json: 2,521 of 3,293 products are vendor Alessandro Design, mostly lighting (Candelabre Cristal 500, Lustre LED cu Telecomanda 465, and so on). So for an AI summary, the file drops the brand's main selling point.

What I refuted:
- "Contradict the brand" goes too far. The file says nothing false and never denies manufacturing.
- The same /pages/companie describes itself in seller terms: "Ne specializăm în vânzarea de corpuri de iluminat", "ne-am remarcat prin comercializarea de produse", "nu este doar un magazin online". So DWF's wording matches the site's own copy. An agent asked "do they make their own products?" would find nothing either way, and the file links /pages/companie.
- The practical effect is small. It is DWF's text and it only affects how AI tools describe the company. It is not a blocker.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. It only replaces line 13. The summary on line 3 (the part llms.txt readers weight most) and line 43 keep the seller framing.
2. It suggests Marcello Funghi and Korman Technik are outside brands. The site never says that. Its own evidence cuts the other way: the "Producator direct" block also shows on Marcello Funghi (eclat) and Korman Technik (glanz) mirrors, and a blog post says the mirrors are "fabricate ... în propria fabrică". The fix would add a new, unverified claim.
3. The CUI and legal-entity detail are not needed for this point. RO43286659 is correct, though; it appears on the site's SEAP page.

The 2023 vs 2024 factory year conflict is a problem on the site's pages, not in llms.txt. The fix should simply leave the year out.
verdict.better_fix:
Only after the client confirms the claim, make an additive change and keep DWF's accurate seller wording. In templates/llms.txt.liquid:
(a) Add a link to the "Despre Alessandro Design" list, after the "Despre companie" item (template line 14): "- [Fabrica Alessandro Design](https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/pages/fabrica-alessandro-design)". The page returned 200 with a self canonical in the v2b-recheck fetch.log and the v2-facts html. Re-run the URL check after adding it.
(b) Add this sentence after template line 19 (body line 13): "Potrivit site-ului, corpurile de iluminat marca Alessandro Design sunt produse în fabrica proprie a companiei din Guzhen (Guangdong, China)."
(c) Optionally, change body line 43 / template line 49 to "Alessandro Design produce și comercializează corpuri de iluminat pentru ...".
Leave out the factory year (the site says 2023 on one page and 2024 on another), and leave out any statement about who owns Marcello Funghi or Korman Technik. If the client does not want "China" in the AI summary, drop "din Guzhen (Guangdong, China)" and keep only the link.

verified.problem: Needs client decision. Line 231 tells agents to rely on the Help Center and the official site pages for orders, delivery, returns and warranty. The file now links both the Terms of Service and the new refund policy, and these sources contradict each other on return terms, shipping rates and contact details.
verified.evidence: ToS (v2-facts/html/tos.txt line 540): 'în termen de 10 zile, să denunțe unilateral Contractul'; line 552: 'cheltuielile de returnare sunt suportate de consumator'. Fresh /policies/refund-policy (10:12:56Z): 'Produsele pot fi returnate in termen de 14 zile' and 'Returul este gratuit'. The shipping policy says 'Costul livrării este de 35.99 lei' and '45.99 lei' for EU countries, while Help article 5429 gives different per-country rates. The SEAP Help article gives the email 'contact@alessandro.salehero.ro' (help-articles-cached.md line 820).
verified.fix: The client fixes the legacy ToS clause, the shipping-policy rates and the SEAP article email. Until then, optionally make body line 231 (template 237) name the source of truth for returns, e.g.: 'Pentru condițiile de retur, sursa de referință este Politica de retur (https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/policies/refund-policy); pentru restul informațiilor despre comenzi, livrare și garanții, utilizați Help Center-ul.'

verdict.reasoning:
I checked this against the saved fetches and made no new requests. The site does have some inconsistent content, but the llms.txt change did not cause any of it, and the finding overstates how much the linked pages disagree.

1. Where the text and links came from (dwf-vs-final.diff). Line 231 ("Pentru informații actualizate ... Help Center-ul și informațiile oficiale") is DWF's original sentence, unchanged. The Terms of Service and shipping policy links were also in DWF's file. The only link we added in that block is /policies/refund-policy.

2. The refund policy link we added agrees with the Help Center, which line 231 names as the place to look. Fresh refund-policy fetch (content-review/policies_refund_policy.body): 14 days, return is free (no pickup or processing fee), and shipping is withheld on "subjective" returns (21.99 RON when shipping was free). Help articles 11295 and 11294 (v2b-recheck/help-articles-cached.md lines 558-600 and 906-960) say the same: 14 days, free pickup and processing, shipping deducted only for subjective returns. So the link we added supports the Help Center rather than contradicting it.

3. The Terms of Service evidence is misread. Line 540 is an old clause citing OG 130/2000 / Legea 51/2003 with a 10-day period. Line 552, which the finding also quotes, is in the ToS's own "Politica de Retur" section. It says "14 zile calendaristice" twice and sends readers to the dedicated return policy page. So the 10-day clause conflicts only with the rest of the same document; the ToS return section, the refund policy and the Help Center all agree on 14 days. The only real wording difference is "cheltuielile de returnare sunt suportate de consumator" versus "Returul este gratuit". Even that matches in practice, because the refund policy withholds the shipping cost on subjective returns. The finding quoted "gratuit" and left that part out.

4. Shipping rates. /policies/shipping-policy (v2-facts/html/shipping.txt lines 519-528) gives the Romanian rate as 21.99 lei, free over 400 lei. Help article 5429 gives the same. The two differ only for BG/HU/GR/PL/CZ and similar countries. Buyers there use their own ccTLD sites, where llms.txt is only a pointer to agents.md. The shipping link came from DWF.

5. Contact details. The SEAP Help article with contact@alessandro.salehero.ro and WhatsApp 0723 029 676 is not linked from llms.txt. The llms.txt contact block (021.555.7252, WhatsApp 0730.478.880, contact@alessandrodesign.ro) matches /pages/contact and /pages/achizitii-publice-seap (v2-facts/html/contact.txt lines 510-514, seap.txt lines 553-558).

Net: none of these conflicts comes from the theme change, and the one link we added reduces confusion. An agent following the footer would reach the same ToS and shipping pages anyway. Rewording line 231 is an optional editorial choice, not a fix for a defect in this change.
verdict.better_fix: No change to templates/llms.txt.liquid is needed. At most, send the client a separate content note (not part of this change): (a) delete or update the old 10-day OG 130/2000 clause in the ToS "Responsabilitatea" section (tos.txt line 540); (b) bring the foreign-country rates in the shipping policy (35.99 / 45.99 lei) in line with Help article 5429; (c) fix the email and WhatsApp number in the SEAP Help article (contact@alessandro.salehero.ro, 0723 029 676).

verified.problem: In the merged label, 'cookies' is the English plural. Standard Romanian (DOOM3) and the site's own footer both use 'cookie-uri'. The word came from DWF's original label 'Politica de cookies', but the line was rewritten, so it can be fixed now.
verified.evidence: Body line 227: '- [Politica de confidențialitate și cookies](https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/policies/privacy-policy)'. Fresh footer on every page (10:11-10:12Z): 'Politica de utilizare cookie-uri', linking to /policies/privacy-policy. That the DOOM3 plural is 'cookie-uri' comes from outside knowledge, not the site.
verified.fix: In templates/llms.txt.liquid line 233, change the line to: '- [Politica de confidențialitate și cookie-uri](https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/policies/privacy-policy)'

verdict.reasoning:
The facts in the finding are correct, but the change has no practical effect. It is a wording nit, not a defect.

What I confirmed:
- templates/llms.txt.liquid line 233 and the dev-theme render work/devtest/ro-llms.body line 227 both say "Politica de confidențialitate și cookies". The link goes to /policies/privacy-policy, which returns 200 in final-urlcheck.
- The word came from DWF's original label, dwf-llms.txt line 227 "Politica de cookies".
- The live footer uses "Politica de utilizare cookie-uri" (saved renders in content-review/*.body and v3-spec/home.ro.html). The privacy policy says "module cookie" (v2-facts/html/privacy.txt lines 525-539). The site itself never says "cookies" in visible Romanian text.
- An earlier draft, v3-spec/draft-merged-llms.ro.txt line 111, already used "cookie-uri". The final went back to DWF's word.
- DOOM3 giving the plural "cookie-uri" comes from outside knowledge, as the finding says.

Why it doesn't matter in practice:
- The link, its target and the meaning are all correct. An LLM or crawler reads "cookies" and "cookie-uri" the same way, and the line still points to the page that covers cookies.
- "cookies" is common Romanian web usage. The theme's own stock locale has it: locales/ro.json line 453 "Politica de cookies".
- Other English words sit in the same section and the rest of the file ("Help Center", "Dropshipping", "Showroom"), so this label is not an odd one out.
- No URL, fact, spec or rendering problem follows from it.

Conclusion: this is an optional style polish, not a real problem.
verdict.better_fix: Optional, only to match the footer's wording. In templates/llms.txt.liquid line 233, replace "și cookies" with "și cookie-uri". This is the one-word change the finding proposes, and it matches the earlier draft v3-spec/draft-merged-llms.ro.txt line 111. It needs no other change and has no effect on URLs.
